title: Dietary arginine drives codon-dependent MHC class I translation and improves immunity in colon tumorigenesis and respiratory viral infection.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and parsed the only processed file the paper deposited: GSE322652_tRNA_counts_isoacceptor_final.tsv.gz (1.5 kB compressed) from the NCBI GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus) FTP site. It is a single table of 48 cytoplasmic transfer-RNA isoacceptor rows by 8 sample columns (4 arginine-fed, 4 arginine-restricted RKO colon cancer cells), 384 integer read counts, no duplicate row names, no mitochondrial transfer RNAs. I confirmed the paper's headline tRNA result in the file: all five arginine isoacceptors fall under restriction (ratios 0.58-0.92) while total library counts are nearly equal (53.1M vs 52.1M). I also checked NCBI links from the PubMed record (PMID 42532044): exactly one GEO series and one BioProject (PRJNA1430810, 8 sequencing runs), and searched GEO for other 2026 arginine-restriction series - the two hits found belong to different papers (GSE324976 Epstein-Barr virus, GSE310301 4T1 breast tumors, PMID 41511309).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the mouse diet experiments, influenza and SARS-CoV-2 infection, colon tumorigenesis, synonymous codon mutants, ribosome stalling at arginine codons and MHC (major histocompatibility complex) class I protein levels comes from the abstract and press coverage only. The paper is paywalled, not in PubMed Central, so I could not read the data availability statement, methods or supplementary table list; Europe PMC reports no open-access full text and no supplementary files.

a1_downloadable.note: Open GEO FTP download, no login or application; I fetched the 1.5 kB gzipped TSV successfully.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No prediction target column exists. The interesting label - how strongly a gene's translation is repressed by arginine shortage - is nowhere in the deposit; it would have to be built from ribosome profiling or proteomics that was never deposited.

a3_inputs_present.note: No sequences and no gene-level data. The file holds 48 isoacceptor names (e.g. cyto-Arg-TCT) and counts; any codon or messenger-RNA sequence features would have to come entirely from outside resources.

a4_units_stated.note: Values are raw sequencing read counts, consistent across all 8 columns; units are implied by the file name rather than documented, but unambiguous.

a5_enough_rows.note: 48 transfer-RNA isoacceptor rows and 8 samples = 384 numbers total, from one cell line and two conditions. The checklist needs about 1,500 labelled rows, or 400 for classification.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially small; fits in memory thousands of times over.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: GEO metadata says 8 samples and the file has exactly 8 sample columns. The paper itself is paywalled so no independent count to compare against.

a8_label_provenance.note: Counts are direct YAMAT-seq (a transfer-RNA sequencing protocol) measurements, not another model's output; the fed/restricted condition label is the experimental design.

existing_models.name: Riboclette (Communications Biology 2025, PMID 41299006; code at github.com/fcraighero/riboclette)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved - I read the abstract and summary only, not the performance table or the split definition.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: From the abstract: they identify codons of the deprived amino acid, poly-basic stretches and negatively charged residues as stalling drivers, and frame motif-level causal attribution as the open interpretability problem. I did not read their discussion.

backbone.name: None applicable - no sequence-level data to embed

integration.partner_dataset: None viable from this deposit alone
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written: 48 isoacceptor counts carry no gene, protein or variant identifier to join on.

controls.positive_control: The arginine isoacceptor drop is itself a clean positive control and I verified it in the file (all 5 arginine isoacceptors down 0.58-0.92x), but it is a two-group comparison, not a modelling task.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is possible but meaningless at n=8 samples.
controls.external_validation: None deposited; no second cell line, tissue or condition in this series.

honest_claim_h3: With this deposit a model could claim nothing beyond 'four arginine-restricted RKO cell cultures have fewer arginine transfer-RNA reads than four fed cultures', which is a t-test, not a model.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a gene's codon composition to predict how much arginine shortage shuts down its protein production.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would need, per human gene, the coding sequence (codon counts, especially the six arginine codons) plus how much its translation changes when arginine is scarce. The deposited data provides neither: it has 48 transfer-RNA isoacceptor rows and 8 samples, no genes.
plain_idea.predict: Change in ribosome occupancy or protein level per gene under arginine restriction, measured by ribosome profiling or mass spectrometry. Neither assay was deposited for this paper, so the true answer does not exist in the released data.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Immunologists and cancer-metabolism labs would want to know which other immune genes besides MHC (major histocompatibility complex) class I are arginine-sensitive, to pick targets for dietary or arginase-blocking therapy. But that question needs the gene-level assays this paper kept behind the paywall.

more_or_better_data.why: 48 isoacceptor rows from one cell line versus Riboclette's training set of ribosome profiling across six amino acid deprivation conditions and thousands of transcripts.

confidence_score.why: Four replicates per condition is enough to estimate noise for a t-test but nowhere near enough to calibrate per-prediction uncertainty for any model.

models_beatable.why: Riboclette is a 2025 deep learning model with open code on GitHub covering exactly the amino-acid-deprivation stalling question; we have no competing data to beat it with.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails the first condition: our data measures transfer-RNA abundance, not the ribosome footprints Riboclette predicts, so it cannot even be used in the same evaluation.

ml_idea: The scientifically interesting task - predict per-gene translational sensitivity to arginine shortage from codon usage - cannot be built from this deposit. It would need the paper's unreleased ribosome profiling or proteomics. A workaround (pull public amino-acid-deprivation ribosome profiling from GEO and model it) would be a different project that does not use this paper's data at all, and Riboclette already did it.

effort.compute_note: Measured directly: the whole deposit is a 1.5 kB gzipped TSV that parses in milliseconds. Compute is a non-issue; there is simply nothing to compute on.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the rows in the single GEO supplementary file. 48 isoacceptors by 8 samples kills it in under a minute - which is exactly what happened.

verdict_reason: The only data released is a 48-row by 8-sample transfer-RNA count table (1.5 kB). Fails A5 (far under 400 rows), A2 (no target column) and A3 (no sequences or gene-level inputs). The mouse diet, infection, tumorigenesis, ribosome-stalling and MHC class I protein results that make the paper interesting have no corresponding public dataset, and the paper is paywalled so even the data availability statement is unreadable. Verified by downloading and parsing the file.
